searchText: Hey <@774033563732541451> any notable updates on PQ registration system contracts with sig verifications? Ready in https://github.com/ethereum/pq-staking-contracts PR related to optimizations: https://github.com/ethereum/pq-staking-contracts/pull/11 . Some comments there, but merged. After did an Ethlib PR with more comprehensive test vectors since existing ones were quite weak https://github.com/ethereum/EthLib/pull/2643 (merged) Upsyreamrd new test vectors into the contract repo https://github.com/ethereum/pq-staking-contracts/pull/13 (merged) So basically the repo has quite decent version with PoP and decent test vectors. I'm planning to FV the signature verification but that's medium term plus. Summary of gas costs with PoP https://github.com/ethereum/pq-staking-contracts/blob/main/contracts/README.md#gas-of-the-proof-of-possession Amazing work. Thank you! 🙏 an extra 59,776 gas for the proof is very reasonable. It's like ~$0.10 right now. Follow up question, what's the system contract fee structure like? Does it mirror what potuz proposed? Will it allow many validators/builders to register PQ data before a fork starts consuming them? Also, would it be okay for us to list you as an author of this EIP? yes, it's the EIP's fee logic, unchanged. the contracts are a Solidity port of the bytecode in potuz's PR, and the only addition is the PoP signature appended to the request calldata. I added tests that send every call to both the EIP's original bytecode in the text, and this new version, and check that they agree on success, return data, logs, storage and balance. They're synced to the current head of the EIP PR (20e8d37), and have a quick script to update (although i think it will be temporal if PoP ends up being part of the EIP). The only difference is gas, since each request now carries the 2.4KB signature -- although that's pretty obvious ha sure. might be also worth considering main authors of 8450... since this PoP idea comes from there. so maybe also add <@427491045308235776> and <@923866336382316594> if they're okay with it. I'm totally fine with this on my side 🙂 <@774033563732541451> ah I just noticed that we only sign over the xmss pubkey part of the message, not the vrf root. I was hoping we'd sign over the whole `pq_data` but maybe this is fine. I would need to remove the VRF uniqueness check in the request handler. Otherwise an attacker could front-run your request with the same VRF root. <@427491045308235776> is it okay for two validators to have the same VRF root? I think it would be very bad practice. Bad enough that we should disallow it entirely? Sorry, missed sharing this convo about exactly that point: https://github.com/ethereum/pq-staking-contracts/pull/9#discussion_r4569612885 From the contract perspective, it is just including it and we could call it a day. not sure adds much to it since there is no asked PoP of the VRF root. But if asking for uniqueness feels safer, maybe that's fine. not sure i have strong opinion. just left some open thoughts ^ Maybe only this highlight i wrote: > I think the only upside is that you could reuse the signature again to register another VRF root... including VRF root in M forces you to change the xmss pubkey. But tbh, not sure we might care about facilitating this and is always better to ask for a new xmss pubkey when re-registering. I would feel better if we signed over it too. Because it will defeat a front-running attack. And allow us to enforce uniqueness. This is assuming CL requires uniqueness of VRF root, no? If so, agree. Yes, that's already the case in the spec PR. Cool, then I'll change to include the VRF root in the signed message, just to make all things coherent. We can still keep it open for discussion but better for things to be coherent for now. It is easy to change later if someone else has a good argument to rollback. Sounds good, thank you! Please ping me whenever that's ready. I'm working to integrate your changes into Potuz's EIP pull request. Also, do you think it's fine to just include the solidity in the EIP? Not sure I want to convert it back to eas. I don't have a strong opinion tbh. Not sure which are best pratices on this. Maybe we can include whatever feels good now, and when things feel more solid we can transform in whatever is the best thing (geas, raw bytecode, keep solidity, etc). Not sure I expect much to change, but maybe isn't that important now the format. Even if FVed which I plan to explore doing it; i think this will require some audit eventually. Yep agreed. Let’s go with solidity for now. mm if cl requires vrf uniqueness. what stops the frontrunning then? because we arent doing the PoP of the VRF root anyway, no? You send register (jtraglia_xmss_pubkey_A, vrf_root_1) Then I front run you with (my_xmss_pubkey_B, vrf_root_1) mines goes first and you are doomed, no? Maybe worth thinking if we really need VRF root uniqueness in CL and why. Unless we ask for a PoP of the VRF root in the EL contract, the signing of it in the message I don't think solves that property (if required). mmm maybe we can: 1. drop uniqueness check in CL when registering 2. mandate that the VRF leaves be `leaf_i = H(secret_i ‖ xmss_pubkey ‖ i)` So it becomes clear who copied who hwen the VRF root is revealed for duties? if i copied your VRF root: 1. I can't clearly create the proof because I don't know your secrets 2. if you revealed your leaf and I simply copy your proofs, it will still mention your xmss pub key which isn't mine .. so I'm slashed/ejected or something 😅 (sharing early thought for consideration, haven't thought if has any negative consequence for CL logic or mechancis) Sorry, I was eating lunch. Err you're right. I think we're just going to need to drop the uniqueness check in the CL. There is a situation in which someone registers two validators with the same VRF root. Obviously, that would be pretty bad. But it should only negatively affect them. i feel this is a cheap tuning that allow us to decide if want to discourage this situation. we're free to decide if we want to do something or not at the CL layer. but binds the xmss pubkey to the VRF root. Yeah we can evaluate things like that. So for now, your system contracts are fine. Sorry for the confusion! My bad 😄 No problem. I think was a good question Made this PR for the EIP: * https://github.com/potuz/EIPs/pull/4 And made this commit for the CL specs: * https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5809/changes/cdfd8598e9c935cb6500622fd0f796afb4d94f8f Yeah it’s fine imo If you copy my vrf, then you would not be able to propose without knowing how to generate it for example oh this moved quite a bit, <@592004585506340885> reviewing now and merging, if everyone here gave already the OK And I told you in private, but thank you for this JT and others did a lot very quickly! you did not add other authors, but I think after this merges you can add yourself I mean only Ignacio was added Ok, the "opaque" thing is really gone now lol Yes, I thought Ignacio did most of the work here 😄 the POP idea itself didn't warrant being added as an author imo. Approved and merged with a single comment that I didn't like what I assume Claude decided as a section title... but merged it anyway Mostly yeah, but one nice thing is that from the CL's perspective it's still mostly opaque. If the signature scheme or whatever change, we'd just need to deploy a different system contract. Yes, but note what i [mentioned earlier.](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1570771708137312327/1573064120155115593) Point 2. situation is something that could happen (with low prob), and that tuning of the VRF definition could solve it. (Edit: doesn't change the conclusion, just a trick we can use if we want to detect the situation in the CL and do something to the one that copied it) Honestly I thought we were going to see a pushback from pools, this is why I was reticent...

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: Hey <@774033563732541451> any notable updates on PQ registration system contracts with sig verifications?

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content:
Ready in https://github.com/ethereum/pq-staking-contracts

PR related to optimizations: https://github.com/ethereum/pq-staking-contracts/pull/11 . Some comments there, but merged.

After did an Ethlib PR with more comprehensive test vectors since existing ones were quite weak https://github.com/ethereum/EthLib/pull/2643 (merged)

Upsyreamrd new test vectors into the contract repo https://github.com/ethereum/pq-staking-contracts/pull/13 (merged)

So basically the repo has quite decent version with PoP and decent test vectors.

I'm planning to FV the signature verification but that's medium term plus.

Summary of gas costs with PoP https://github.com/ethereum/pq-staking-contracts/blob/main/contracts/README.md#gas-of-the-proof-of-possession

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: Amazing work. Thank you! 🙏  an extra 59,776 gas for the proof is very reasonable. It's like ~$0.10 right now.

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: Follow up question, what's the system contract fee structure like? Does it mirror what potuz proposed? Will it allow many validators/builders to register PQ data before a fork starts consuming them?

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: Also, would it be okay for us to list you as an author of this EIP?

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content:
yes, it's the EIP's fee logic, unchanged. the contracts are a Solidity port of the bytecode in potuz's PR, and the only addition is the PoP signature appended to the request calldata. 
I added tests that send every call to both the EIP's original bytecode in the text, and this new version, and check that they agree on success, return data, logs, storage and balance. They're synced to the current head of the EIP PR (20e8d37), and have a quick script to update (although i think it will be temporal if PoP ends up being part of the EIP).

The only difference is gas, since each request now carries the 2.4KB signature -- although that's pretty obvious ha

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content: sure. might be also worth considering main authors of 8450... since this PoP idea comes from there. so maybe also add <@427491045308235776>  and <@923866336382316594> if they're okay with it.

From the contract perspective, it is just including it and we could call it a day. not sure adds much to it since there is no asked PoP of the VRF root.
But if asking for uniqueness feels safer, maybe that's fine. not sure i have strong opinion. just left some open thoughts ^

> I think the only upside is that you could reuse the signature again to register another VRF root... including VRF root in M forces you to change the xmss pubkey. But tbh, not sure we might care about facilitating this and is always better to ask for a new xmss pubkey when re-registering.

excerpts.author: jtraglia

excerpts.author: jtraglia

excerpts.author: jtraglia

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content: Cool, then I'll change to include the VRF root in the signed message, just to make all things coherent. We can still keep it open for discussion but better for things to be coherent for now. It is easy to change later if someone else has a good argument to rollback.

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: Sounds good, thank you! Please ping me whenever that's ready. I'm working to integrate your changes into Potuz's EIP pull request.

excerpts.author: jtraglia
excerpts.content: Also, do you think it's fine to just include the solidity in the EIP? Not sure I want to convert it back to eas.

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content: I don't have a strong opinion tbh. Not sure which are best pratices on this. Maybe we can include whatever feels good now, and when things feel more solid we can transform in whatever is the best thing (geas, raw bytecode, keep solidity, etc). Not sure I expect much to change, but maybe isn't that important now the format.

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content: Even if FVed which I plan to explore doing it; i think this will require some audit eventually.

excerpts.author: jtraglia

excerpts.author: jsign

excerpts.author: jsign
excerpts.content:
mmm maybe we can:
1. drop uniqueness check in CL when registering
2. mandate that the  VRF leaves be `leaf_i = H(secret_i ‖ xmss_pubkey ‖ i)`

So it becomes clear who copied who hwen the VRF root is revealed for duties?
